newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET - Cairns still wants to be an allrounder.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - Cairns still wants to be an allrounder.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Feb 24 - Key New Zealand player Chris Cairns doesn't want to be half an international cricketer, NZPA reports.
Cairns the allrounder has been reduced to Cairns the batsman by a lingering ankle injury he picked up playing in a testimonial match for New Zealand team-mate Gavin Larsen at the start of February.
He has turned his bowling from lively fast-medium into barely adequate medium pace so he played in yesterday's one-day international against England at Eden Park solely as a batsman.
It worked well, as Cairns hammered 79 off 76 balls to top-score for New Zealand in their six-wicket loss.
But while Cairns conceded he is unlikely to bowl again in this one-day series, which has three games to go, he doesn't want to give up half his game.
"When you're an allrounder it's mentally very demanding to switch onto whatever aspect you're trying to do," Cairns said last night.
"It is a tough job but very rewarding."
Cairns says while it's not necessarily easier to be simply a batsman or bowler, "it is easier to prepare".
But it's something he wants to persevere with. He's determined not to be reduced to being solely a batsman if he can help it.
"If I can't bowl I'll try to bat. Some people have had a crack at me and say 'what are you doing playing?'.
"But I love to play; I want to be on the field playing."
Cairns said the injury had been frustrating but he believes he hasn't lost any of his pace when fully fit.
"It's inhibiting me from bowling. It's an impact injury, it's happened in county cricket and it's happened for New Zealand before.
"It doesn't disable me from batting. But there's more stress with bowling than batting."
He has scored 1398 runs at 27 in one-dayers and taken 23 expensive wickets.
Cairns hopes he'll be able to bowl when the two-test series starts against Sri Lanka in Dunedin next month.
"It's a case of trying it every day. The way I was bowling was a joke and I wasn't doing justice to myself or the team. If I'm not 100 percent, or close to it, there's no point bowling.
"But I'll be trying to bowl in the tests."
